title: Practical microscale HTE in 96-well vial plates (Suzuki-type screening workflow)
summary: A bench-practical recipe for running reaction arrays at 10 umol scale in glass vial inserts held in 96-well metal blocks. Reagents are dosed as stock solutions, the block is inerted and sealed, heated with tumble stirring, then diluted into daughter plates for fast UPLC analysis. Cross-couplings such as Suzuki-Miyaura are the typical use case.

steps.text: Make stock solutions of substrates, catalysts, ligands and bases (roughly 0.1 M for substrate) rather than weighing solids per well; use pre-dosed catalyst/reagent libraries if available.
Place 8 x 30 mm glass vial inserts in a 96-well metal block (about 100 uL per reaction, 20 uL in 4 x 21 mm inserts if material is scarce).
Dose the stock solutions into the vials with multichannel pipettes or a liquid handler, working inside a glovebox if the chemistry is air-sensitive.
Seal the block (cap mat or sealing film; pressure vessel if a reactive gas is needed).
Heat the block on a plate heater with tumble stirring (or vortex shaking) for the set reaction time.

duration_s.note: Source gives no time; reaction time depends on chemistry.

steps.text: Quench and dilute an aliquot from every well into a daughter plate using a multichannel pipette; remove volatile solvents with a vacuum centrifuge or filter solids through a filter plate if needed.
Analyse each well by reverse-phase UPLC(-MS) with a fast gradient; the source quotes a few minutes per sample.

duration_s.note: 'a few minutes per sample' paraphrased; 3 min taken as midpoint.

equipment.name: 96-well metal block with glass vial inserts

materials: Aryl halide, boronic acid, Pd catalyst/ligand, base stocks (Suzuki example)
safety: Flammable solvents; handle Pd catalysts and bases in a ventilated enclosure.
